sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Maternity and Infant Care Commodities

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Central America Association Agreement (Panama is a Party)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 on Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism, as amended and supplemented by Law No. 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree No. 1 of 2019; Law No. 52 of 2016 on economic substance requirements; regulations and circulars of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Dirección General de Sujetos No Financieros (DGSNF); Public Registry of Panama beneficial ownership register requirements under the Unified Legal Persons Beneficial Ownership Register (RLB) system.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Fully Notarized Copy of Beneficial Owner's Passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport Authority of the Beneficial Owner's Country of Origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Proof of Residential Address of Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility Provider or Financial Institution in Country of Residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Conduct / Criminal Record Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Police or Designated Judicial Authority of the Beneficial Owner's Country of Origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under Law 23/2015 and UAF standards; mandatory screening against OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Panamanian domestic list published by the UAF; real-time continuous monitoring for potential matches during the pre-incorporation phase and prior to any bank account onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Portal de Servicios en Línea (www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official name clearance forms and registry records are processed in Spanish. The proposed legal name may be in any language using the Latin alphabet; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Spanish/Latin alphabet before filing. The name must contain the phrase 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Private Interest Foundation' or the abbreviation 'PIF' to identify the entity type. Brand names of the e-commerce business may be registered separately as trade names or trademarks, but the statutory entity name must satisfy Panamanian naming conventions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its designated resident agent may file a written administrative reconsideration request within 10 working days to the Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá. The request must include a new name proposal or evidence of distinctive branding to overcome the objection. If denied, an appeal may be brought before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Supreme Court of Justice within 30 working days, and a precautionary name reservation may be requested concurrently.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for this industry only insofar as the Private Interest Foundation maintains a statutory registered office in Panama at the address of its designated resident agent (a licensed law firm or services company). The virtual office may serve as the operational mailing address, but it does not replace the mandatory Panamian registered office. For pure online e-commerce of low-risk maternity and baby supplies, physical commercial substance in Panama is not indicated; however, the entity must comply with Law 52 of 2016 economic substance norms if it conducts offshore business management in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Less than 5% annual probability for a low-risk, non-licensed, online-only maternity and baby supply e-commerce entity with no physical inventory or local operational office; the risk increases to approximately 15–20% if the entity registers as a management company or permits third-party nominee services.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of the Registro Público for name search and clearance voucher issuance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Legalization of Beneficial Owner Documents (Passport, Address Proof, Criminal Record) with Apostille

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial and apostille tariffs of the country of issuance; market benchmark of USD 20–40 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva) and Regulations (Reglamento/Estatutos)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian Licensed Attorney / Registered Resident Agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard PIF instruments without complex trust or wealth-protection clauses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry Registration Fee for Private Interest Foundation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry fee for incorporation of a Private Interest Foundation (Fundación de Interés Privado)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident Agent Registration and First-Year Annual Agent Fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk online e-commerce foundation; includes custody of statutory records and registered office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial Beneficial Ownership Register Filing (RLB Registry) and UAF Compliance Package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Sujetos No Financieros (DGSNF) / Unidad de Análisis Financiero

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Standard or Low-Risk merchant entity due diligence package in Panama

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by the tax transparency and economic substance regime (Ley No. 70 de 2019) and supplementary beneficial-ownership decrees. Core formation provisions: Articulos 1-24 (Foundation Charter, Foundation Council, Protector, Beneficiaries, duration); Articulo 25 (legal effects of registration). Implementing rules: Reglamento de Fundaciones de Interes Privado under the Public Registry tariff regimen.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Carta Fundacional (Foundation Charter), protocolized before a Panamanian Notary Public and filed for inscription; accompanied by the Reglamento (Foundation Bylaws) where kept separate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Law 25; the Foundation Charter must declare an initial endowment, customarily nominal USD 10,000 or less. No escrow account impound is required by Panamanian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL. Panama City, Republic of Panama. WHEREAS the Founder constituted [PA_PIF Foundation] under Law No. 25 of 1995 and endowed its initial assets; NOW, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. The initial endowment is accepted and recorded. 2. The registered office is adopted at [complete Panama address], Corregimiento de Bella Vista, Panama City. 3. The Foundation Council is constituted: [Chairman], [Secretary], [Treasurer]. 4. [RegisteredAgent] is appointed Resident Agent for the Republic of Panama. 5. The Foundation Bylaws are adopted; the Protector, if designated, is confirmed. 6. Members are authorized to open bank accounts and to structure the operating e-commerce subsidiary. DATED this ___ day of ______, 20___.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualified Panamanian attorney enrolled with the Colegio Nacional de Abogados; name reservation through Registro Publico de Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to reserve a foundation name, verify ISIC 4791 e-commerce scope under the Foundation Charter's purpose clause, and draft the Charter and Bylaws including beneficiary, protector, and asset endowment clauses; complete the client due diligence file under Ley No. 23 de 2015.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of Founder and proposed Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit with alternative name where the Public Registry flags unavailability; amend purpose clause to match the private-interest foundation limitation on commercial activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Protocolization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder or appointed attorney executes the Carta Fundacional before a Panamanian notary; the notary verifies legal capacity, notarizes signatures, and protocolizes the instrument into the notarial register for subsequent presentation to the Registro Publico.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney where Founder is absent
Notarial coversheet (cabecera) prepared by law firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Execute an addendum in the same protocol where the notary detects drafting deficiencies; re-notarize if instrument is rejected or materially altered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Publico de Panama - Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the protocolized Foundation Charter via the Registry's electronic filing queue or counter, pay the applicable tariff, and obtain the Certificate of Registration (Inscripcion) evidencing the foundation's existence and legal capacity from registration.
required_dossiers: Tax identification of presenting law firm
Poder of Resident Agent if representation is delegated
step_by_step_formation_sop.pendencia: within the notice term by filing corrected pages; request expedited examination for standardized Charter templates; escalate to the Registry Directorate where examination exceeds statutory timelines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RUC Tax Registration and Municipal Aviso de Operacion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economia y Finanzas; Municipalidad de Panama - Direccion de Aviso de Operacion
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the RUC through the DGI e-portal, then apply for the municipal Aviso de Operacion under Ley No. 66 de 2018 for the foundation's registered office or operating e-commerce subsidiary; register the business address with municipal treasury.
required_dossiers: Lease or title of registered office
Foundation Bylaws and Council Resolution No. 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify RUC data inconsistencies via DGI correction queue; resubmit municipal application with certified registration documents; request administrative exemption where the foundation is strictly a holding vehicle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Franchise Tax and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGI - Tasa Unica Anual; Registro Unico de Beneficiarios Finales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial annual franchise tax declaration (Tasa Unica Anual) and pay the current USD 300 tariff through the DGI e-tax platform; submit the final beneficial ownership declaration to the Registro Unico de Beneficiarios Finales within the statutory window.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt for Tasa Unica Anual
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to DGI validation queries and amend the beneficial ownership declaration; file corrective return without prejudice to late-payment surcharge; maintain evidence of timely submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account and Payment Rail Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama (regulated commercial banks); PSP aggregators for Stripe/PayPal onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pass a Foundation Council resolution authorizing bank account opening and signatories; complete bank KYC under Ley No. 23 de 2015; engage a Panama-licensed payment processor to onboard Stripe and PayPal rails for the operating subsidiary's online maternity and infant-care store.
required_dossiers: KYC forms with beneficial owner and PEP declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Supply supplemental source-of-funds documentation where the bank queries beneficial ownership; reroute payment traffic through the operating subsidiary if the PSP declines the foundation as merchant.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial license applies to pure e-commerce of baby and maternity supplies (ISIC 4791 non-manufacturing). Horizontal operating authorities: Municipalidad de Panama - Direccion General de Avisos de Operacion; MITRADEL for workplace registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operacion (Municipal Operating Notice) pursuant to Ley No. 66 de 2018; no separate manufacturing or statutory commercial license is required for online retail of maternity and infant-care commodities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Direccion de Evaluacion Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (low-impact commercial and warehousing operations): simple environmental registration suffices under the national EIA procedure of Ley No. 41 de 1998 and its implementing regulation. Full EIA Report (Category III) is not triggered for a flagship e-commerce fulfillment center below the regulated area thresholds; verification of surface area is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC-intensive emissions in pure e-commerce. Sanitary wastewater must meet MiAMBIENTE effluent quality criteria and municipal sewer ordinances; solid waste handled under the national integrated waste management rules administered by MiAMBIENTE; indoor air and occupational VOC exposure maintained within ACGIH TLV limits; no ozone-depleting substances in cold-chain equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Visto Bueno del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panama (fire-safety clearance: extinguishers, emergency exits, and alarm systems) for the registered office and any warehouse; municipal structural and occupancy permit (Permiso de Ocupacion) from the Direccion de Obras of the Municipality of Panama; mandatory employer registration with MITRADEL for workplace safety and with the Caja de Seguro Social for payroll and occupational accident coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); online portal: SIME (sistema.gob.pa) / dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) by submitting the Private Interest Foundation charter, evidence of legal existence, notarized and apostilled documents, and proof of appointment of a local resident agent/fiscal representative. The application is lodged through the DGI's SIME (Integrated Revenue Management System) portal and results in a permanent RUC for tax declaration purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable (no check-the-box election). Panama's territorial system taxes only Panamanian-source income. A PIF may elect simplified small-taxpayer treatment for local-source commercial activities if annual gross receipts do not exceed USD 36,000; otherwise it is automatically under the general ITBMS regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 36,000 in annual taxable gross receipts for the simplified small-taxpayer election; mandatory RUC/ITBMS registration is required for any person or legal entity engaged in taxable activities with Panamanian nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates real-time electronic invoicing through the DGI's SIME platform or DGI-approved technological providers. E-invoices must be validated in real time, carry a unique invoice code (VUC), digital stamp (hash/QR), and fiscal authorization before issuance. Non-compliance results in invoice rejection and potential RUC suspension.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods and qualifying exported services are taxable at 0% ITBMS where the goods are transferred and shipped abroad to a non-resident purchaser within the statutory timeframe, and where the seller holds documentary evidence of the foreign sale, physical export, and receipt of payment from a non-resident account.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger retrospective clawback of the 7% ITBMS, a penalty of up to 200% of the evaded tax, default surcharges and interest, and criminal prosecution under Panama's Tax Code and antifraud statutes. Customs authorities may also impose fines and suspend the exporter's registration for repeated documentary irregularities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Panama has no conventional central bank and the US Dollar (USD) is full legal tender under Cabinet Decree No. 18 of 1950; Banco Nacional de Panamá operates as the State fiscal agent, while the SBP exclusively licenses and supervises banks and financial entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully dollarized economy with the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) existing only as a currency-unit pegged 1:1 to USD and issued solely as coinage. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible with no prior exchange-control approval, no repatriation permits, and no surrender requirements for trade receipts. Profit remittances and capital distributions from an operating PIF are subject only to the territorial income-tax regime (income sourced outside Panama is exempt) and to the relevant bank's own AML/fintech screening protocols, which creates no de facto conversion hurdle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender or repatriation obligation on export proceeds or foreign-currency receivables. A PIF conducting online cross-border sales may retain USD settlement balances offshore or onshore without central-bank declaration, filing requirement, or exchange-control penalty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC Credomatic (BAC International Bank, Inc.) Panamá

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium under Panamanian law. Panama does not recognize the EU-style 'Electronic Money Institution' license as a distinct banking category; digital payment providers and virtual-asset service providers must register with the SBP under Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT), SBP Agreement 004-2021, and the SBP Fintech Innovation Hub (Framework 001-2022). An offshore digital EMI without a Panamanian SBP registration cannot lawfully hold a Panamanian-domiciled PIF's funds as a local account, although the PIF may use such EMI as a treasury-byproduct rail provided settlement ultimately passes through an SBP-regulated local bank. For the target payment rails (Stripe and PayPal), the PIF should establish the merchant account in the entity's legal name and configure settlement to a Panama Tier-1 USD account; Stripe/PayPal themselves operate as unregulated-in-Panama payment facilitators but do not require a Panamanian EMV license for the merchant of record, which is the PIF.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Panamanian statute absolutely requires physical board attendance for account opening, but SBP-regulated Tier-1 banks condition account activation on a positive KYC interview. In practice, remote video interviews are accepted only for the founder/council member when combined with: (1) apostilled passport/corporate registry documents; (2) a notarized foundation charter (Escritura Pública) inscribed at the Public Registry; (3) an original banker's reference from a correspondent institution; and (4) a formal letter from the licensed resident agent affirming the foundation's legal existence. Most Tier-1 banks still require at least one designated signatory or the appointed Panamanian counsel holding a specific power of attorney to appear physically at a branch interview for final sign-off and for issuance of digital credentials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF lacks economic substance or demonstrates passive/opaque holding behavior
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered foundation charter expressly including 'online retail sales of maternity and infant commodities' as the foundation purpose; Foundation Council resolution appointing the founder/officers; 12-month operational business plan with revenue and settlement forecasts; marketplace integration agreements with Stripe/PayPal/Shopify; supplier pro-forma invoices; executed warehouse/shipping contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity and nominee/foundation concealment red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the registry of beneficial owners (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) maintained by the resident agent; compliant beneficial-ownership file per Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Agreement 002-2021; passport copies of founder, council members, and protector (if any); signed declaration of economic activity and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk counterparties, sanctions exposure, or e-commerce anonymity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative news/sanctions screening report generated by the onboarding bank or a third-party KYC provider; customer/supplier onboarding matrix with identification of the top five suppliers and buyer geographies; PCI-DSS compliance certificate; returns and refund policy; transaction-volume reconciliation report establishing low-risk standard tier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial endowment or operating capital source cannot be verified
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement evidencing the minimum USD 10,000 endowment transferred from a visited bank in the founder's name; verified source-of-funds declaration; prior business bank statement demonstrating the founder's lawful e-commerce revenue; tax-status certificate (RUC / Aviso de Operación) of the founder's origin country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chargeback volatility or inconsistent settlement flows from online payment processors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six-month projected net settlement report; chargeback ratio summary below the bank's tolerance; accepted refunds and dispute-resolution log; third-party payment processor data on tracking numbers and delivery confirmation; audited or accountant-certified revenue recognition policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Domestic USD wire from the founder/investor's verified bank account to the PIF's Panamanian USD account via SWIFT MT103; wire instruction must recite 'Capital Contribution to Private Interest Foundation [name]' and include the foundation registry number; attach the foundation charter, source-of-funds letter, and the sending bank's purpose code for capital transfers (e.g., 'G400' or 'CAPT' as mapped by the correspondent). Panama imposes no FX form, no central-bank authorization, and no stamp duty on inbound capital; USD arrives directly with no conversion. For payment-aggregator settlements (Stripe/PayPal), the inbound settlement is routed under the purpose 'E-commerce goods export proceeds / ISIC 4791' and is processed in USD, equally free of any Panamanian surrender declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails for supplier payments and trade disbursements: SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier wires in USD, EUR, or CNY (MT202 for intermediary/treasury transfers); Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600 ICC) for bulk/seasonal procurement of baby and maternity goods through the Panamanian bank's trade desk; local payment via the Panamanian ACH interbank clearing system (Centro de Procesamiento Interbancario operated by the Panamanian Banking Association) for domestic peso-free settlement. Because the PIF is USD-functional, outflows to USD beneficiaries are costless; non-USD supplier payments aggregate liquidity only at the correspondent bank tier, with no prohibition or license required for such outflows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CNY (CNH) OTC forwards with international dealer banks hedging CNY-denominated supplier payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNY and USD/EUR, cash-settled in USD, offered by Panama's international banking licensees
FX swaps (spot/forward) under ISDA or local master agreements for temporary cross-currency liquidity
Cross-currency interest-rate/principal swaps for USD/CNY restructuring of large-margin supplier purchase facilities

Plain-vanilla USD/CNY and USD/EUR forwards executed with the Tier-1 bank's international treasury section, exempt from local exchange-control and requiring no collateral margin beyond normal credit terms

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Flat Tax (Tasa Única Anual) – B/.300 payment to preserve legal standing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June every calendar year; the date is fixed by statute and is not aligned to the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment generates statutory interest and a 10% surcharge; after three consecutive years of non-payment, the Public Registry may administratively strike off the foundation and it may lose juridical capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) – required only where the Foundation derives Panama-source taxable income under the territorial tax regime; no filing is due for exclusively foreign-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal period, by 31 March of the following year; for an adopted non-calendar fiscal year, within three months of fiscal-year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a fine equal to 5% of the tax due per month of delay, compounded up to 100%, plus a 10% surcharge and monetary correction; continued non-filing may trigger tax collection against foundation assets and culpability of the Foundation Council.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial-Ownership Register Confirmation and Update (confidential registered-agent protocol)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent in Panama at the registered office; DGI Beneficial-Ownership online registry is updated only where a UBO change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually by 30 June, plus within 30 calendar days after any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a current beneficial-ownership register violates Law 23 of 2015 (as amended) and may result in administrative fines of B/.1,000–B/.10,000 and heightened AML/CFT scrutiny of the foundation and its registered agent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit applies to a dormant or passive Private Interest Foundation. An audit becomes compulsory where annual gross Panama-source taxable income exceeds B/.3,000,000, where the foundation is classified as a 'large taxpayer' by the DGI, or where the foundation is separately subject to a sectoral audit requirement (e.g., fiduciary, banking, or securities activity).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panamanian GAAP with IFRS as adopted in Panama for entities required to present full financial statements; simplified IFRS for SMEs / local Panamanian GAAP is permissible for small private foundations not otherwise subject to full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation Council must execute and date an annual confirmation letter each calendar year, delivered to the registered agent by 30 June, verifying the accuracy of the register of founders, Foundation Council members, protector, and ultimate beneficiaries. Any subsequent change must be recorded contemporaneously and, where required, reported to the DGI beneficial-ownership system within 30 calendar days. The register remains confidential, is physically maintained by the registered agent, and is not filed with the Public Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $900–$1,600 per annum (including registered agent, registered office, routine beneficial-ownership maintenance, and administrative support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,800–$3,500 per audit engagement where the B/.3,000,000 threshold is triggered; dormant foundations typically have no audit requirement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard ISR rate) applied to net Panama-source taxable income; alternative minimum tax of 4.67% of gross revenue must be paid when it exceeds the 25% calculation for taxpayers with annual gross income ≥ B/. 3,000,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax model: a PIF's foreign-source income (online sales of baby and maternity supplies settled through Stripe/PayPal abroad, goods fulfilled and delivered outside Panama) is entirely outside the Panamanian income tax base, yielding an effective 0% corporate rate for offshore e-commerce profits; no VAT on exported services; the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime offers reduced effective rates only to qualifying regional headquarters.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 950 (Declaración de Renta – Personas Jurídicas); e-filed through the DGI's T@x Panama digital portal (Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly advance income-tax payments (anticipos) are due during the following fiscal year where the prior-year tax exceeded the statutory minimum.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the last working day of the third month after fiscal year-end (calendar-year legal entities: 31 March); DGI may grant extensions under Tax Code art. 668 on justified application before the original due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All Panama-source gross receipts from the e-commerce business, including online sales of maternity and infant care supplies where goods are sold, delivered, or used in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-source turnover (dropshipping orders fulfilled abroad and settled in Stripe/PayPal outside Panama); the territorial regime requires the PIF to enter only revenues with Panamanian source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 102 – Cost of sales (costo de ventas)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct procurement, inbound freight, warehousing, and delivery costs attributable to the baby/maternity products sold in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support every cost with commercial invoices, DUA import declarations, and bank settlement records; related-party costs must be arm's-length documented for TP purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 103 – Deductible operating expenses (gastos operativos deducibles)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, platform subscription fees, Panama payroll, rent, and DGI-registered expenses directly connected with Panamanian-source operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No deduction is allowed for distributions to foreign beneficiaries, private expenditures of the founder/protector, or expenses allocated to foreign-source profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 104 – Net taxable income (renta neta gravable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 101 minus Boxes 102 and 103, after applying net operating loss carryforwards (up to five years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF derives only foreign-source e-commerce profit, enter zero; retain a territorial-income reconciliation worksheet for DGI inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% of Box 104; when Box 101 exceeds B/. 3,000,000, compare with 4.67% of gross revenue and remit the higher amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A wholly offshore PIF enters zero and must be prepared to prove the absence of Panama-source sales on audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 106 – Advance payments and credits (pagos adelantados y retenciones)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly anticipos, withholding taxes, and other credits recoverable against the annual ISR liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign income taxes paid abroad are not creditable against Panamanian ISR because Panama applies territorial taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 107 – Net tax payable / refund (impuesto a pagar o saldo a favor)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 105 minus Box 106; payment ordered through the DGI's virtual collection module.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Funds must be settled from the PIF's Panamanian bank account; unpaid amounts accrue a 10% monthly surcharge capped at 50%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fine of 5% of the tax due (Tax Code art. 713); late payment: 10% per month or fraction of the unpaid tax, capped at 50%, plus default interest; repeated failures can trigger suspension of the Aviso de Operación, non-issuance of fiscal clearance (paz y salvo), and travel restrictions for responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory WHT on dividends and profit distributions paid out of Panama-source profits; distributions of foreign-source profits by a territorial-scope PIF are exempt from Panamanian WHT; a 5% advance WHT applies to dividend-like advances before formal declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must deliver (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its residence tax authority, (ii) a signed beneficial-ownership and treaty-eligibility declaration, and (iii) substance evidence to the Panamanian withholding agent; the agent files the reduced-rate withholding through T@x Panama and preserves the file for five years. Panama's operative DTAs (Mexico, Chile, South Korea, Portugal, Qatar, Singapore, UAE, Spain, France, Netherlands, among others) commonly reduce dividend WHT to 5–10% for qualifying shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties, license fees, and technical-assistance fees paid to non-residents from Panamanian-source exploitation: 12.5% statutory WHT, reducible to 5–10% under applicable DTAs. Interest paid by a Panamanian debtor to unrelated foreign lenders on foreign-sourced credit: generally 0% WHT (territorial exclusion); qualifying treaty-protected interest may be exempt or capped at 5–10%. No WHT applies to arm's-length settlements for e-commerce platform fees recharged from foreign service providers.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 5,000,000 (five million Panamanian balboas, at parity with USD) in aggregate annual related-party transactions, above which the taxpayer must maintain and file a Local File and related Transfer Pricing Declaration under Executive Decree 171 of 2014; Master File and Country-by-Country Reporting are owed by groups with consolidated revenue ≥ USD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2021, effective 1 January 2022) apply to PIFs and other Panamanian entities conducting 'relevant activities'—including e-commerce distribution—and deriving foreign-source income. The PIF must maintain a registered physical office in Panama, qualified personnel, adequate operating expenditure, and local senior management, and must file an annual economic substance declaration; failures are penalized with progressive administrative fines and can lead to cancellation of the foundation's registration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing or under-reporting Panama-source online maternity-supply sales (for example, routing Stripe/PayPal settlements into opaque foundation bank accounts) or claiming fictitious cost deductions to eliminate Panamanian ISR.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion: imprisonment of 2–5 years and fines of B/. 5,000–B/. 100,000 (Tax Code arts. 770 et seq.); administrative retaliation: 100% surcharge on the evaded tax plus the 10% monthly late-payment surcharge capped at 50%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation-council officers who sign fraudulent returns face joint and several civil restitution, DGI-ordered travel bans (impedimento de salida), seizure of personal assets, and imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the baby-maternity e-commerce business through the PIF with no physical office, no Panamanian staff, no local substance, and undisclosed beneficial ownership while claiming territorial exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 254 of 2021 ESR: administrative fines escalating from B/. 10,000 to B/. 1,000,000; repeated or serious violations cause deregistration of the PIF; DGI may re-characterize the foreign-source income as taxable Panama-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Protectors, council members, and directors can be held personally liable for the fines; aggravating elements lead to director disqualification for up to 3 years and travel-blocking orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML Breach through Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Commingling customer payments from the e-commerce platform with concealed foundation assets, accepting funds through unvetted third-party accounts, or using the Stripe/PayPal proceeds to launder criminal proceeds of third parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama AML/CFT framework (Law 23 of 2015 and Penal Code): imprisonment of 5–12 years, fines of up to B/. 10,000,000, and asset forfeiture; the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) may freeze the foundation's accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and protectors who participated or exhibited willful blindness are criminally liable as co-principals; they face personal asset freezing, extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the Panamanian Transfer Pricing Declaration and Local File after exceeding the B/. 5,000,000 related-party-transaction threshold, or pricing cross-border intercompany purchases of baby supplies outside arm's-length values.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from B/. 1,000 to B/. 25,000 (Tax Code arts. 735, 743–744); DGI may re-determine the taxable income at arm's length and assess additional ISR plus the 10% monthly surcharge (cap 50%).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing incomplete or fraudulent TP documentation are jointly and severally liable for the re-determined tax; false declarations can escalate to criminal penalties for fraud.
